content.title: Executive Summary
content.body: Linear is an issue-tracking and product-planning workspace organized around work items and delivery workflows. It is worth evaluating when a software team wants to connect backlog triage, planning, project status, and day-to-day issue work. This is not a claim of independent structured product review. Validate the workflow with your own backlog, roles, reporting needs, and source-control process before deciding whether Linear fits better than your current system.

content.title: TL;DR
content.body: Consider Linear if your team needs issue tracking and product planning in a shared workflow. Test the requirements that often determine fit: custom fields, permissions, reporting, integrations, notifications, data export, and migration of issue history. Current numeric ratings, review counts, pricing, and plan limits are not independently verified in this review; confirm them directly with Linear before purchasing.

content.title: Feature Evaluation
content.body: Use a representative backlog to evaluate triage, issue ownership, cycles, project status, search, notifications, and links to source-control work. Include routine work and an exception, such as a blocked issue or a cross-team dependency. Record whether users can complete the task without duplicate entry, whether permissions behave as expected, and whether reports answer the questions your team needs. Verify each feature in the plan you would buy.

content.title: Who Should Consider It
content.body: Software teams that want a shared view of issues, planning, and delivery coordination may find Linear worth a pilot. The key question is whether its workflow matches how your team actually plans and ships work. Include developers, project leads, and administrators in the evaluation, and test the process with your real statuses, ownership rules, and reporting requirements before moving the entire backlog.

content.title: Limitations to Test
content.body: Test workflow flexibility, custom fields, roles and permissions, audit needs, reporting, and data export. Migration planning should account for issue history, attachments, labels, comments, relationships, and links to repositories or other tools. Non-engineering teams should also check whether the workflow supports their reporting and approvals without unnecessary workarounds. Treat limitations as test cases, and verify which are current and which depend on plan level.

content.title: Pricing Explained
content.body: Current prices, plan limits, and billing terms are not independently verified here. Check Linear's official pricing page at https://linear.app/pricing and confirm seat rules, included features, usage limits, annual billing, taxes, renewal, and cancellation. Estimate the full cost of the required plan, integrations, administration, onboarding, migration, and ongoing maintenance rather than relying on an entry-tier price.

content.title: Security & Privacy Checks
content.body: Before storing internal or customer data in Linear, review the current security and privacy documentation and contract. Verify authentication, role-based access, data retention and deletion, audit visibility, export, incident notification, and how connected integrations receive access. Confirm which controls are included in the plan you would buy. Use non-sensitive sample data during the pilot and involve the appropriate security or privacy owner for sensitive workflows.

content.title: Implementation Checklist
content.body: Start with a small project or a copy of a representative backlog. Map statuses, teams, ownership, labels, cycles, templates, integrations, permissions, and reports before importing data. Test a sample export and import, compare record counts and relationships, and document anything that needs manual cleanup. Train users on the agreed workflow, assign an administrator, and keep a rollback path until the team has validated critical history and reporting.

content.title: Alternatives
content.body: Compare Linear with alternatives based on the workflow you need, not a universal ranking. Include the products your team already uses and any candidate that meets mandatory requirements for planning, issue tracking, reporting, permissions, and integrations. Run the same task in each product, record missing steps and correction effort, and verify current plan limits. Avoid migrating solely because a competitor has a longer feature list or a different user rating.

content.title: Final Verdict
content.body: Linear is worth shortlisting when issue tracking and product planning are central to a software team's workflow. The decision should depend on a pilot that validates backlog operations, reporting, permissions, integrations, export, and total cost. No independent numeric rating or current price is asserted here. If a mandatory workflow requires repeated workarounds, compare alternatives before migrating critical data.
